title: Your first real script
subtitle: Turn a sequence of commands into a safe, readable tool that fails loudly.
objectives: Write a Bash script with a shebang and strict mode
Use variables, quoting, arguments, and command substitution
Make decisions with test expressions and loops
Handle errors instead of hiding them
Build and run a small system health report

sections.title: A health report you would actually keep

commands.desc: Shebang: select Bash as the interpreter.
Fail fast on errors, unset variables, and pipeline failures.
Run a script from the current directory.
Expand a variable in the shell.
Capture command output in a variable.
Test whether a path is a regular file.

lab.title: Write a health report
lab.scenario: Create a reusable script that another admin could run without reading the source first.

steps.text: Create the script with a shebang and strict mode.
steps.verify: The script should exist at ~/bin/healthcheck.sh and start with #!/bin/bash and set -euo pipefail.

steps.text: Add host, date, kernel, disk, failed-unit, and recent-error sections. Redirect the block to a timestamped file.
steps.verify: Use the complete example above. Quote every variable expansion.

steps.text: Make it executable and run it.
steps.verify: The script should run without errors and print the report path or a summary.

steps.text: Verify the report exists and has content.
steps.verify: The report file should exist under ~/health and include host, date, and disk sections.

steps.text: Break it on purpose: run it with an unwritable report directory and observe the non-zero exit.
steps.verify: The exit status should be non-zero, and the error should be visible.

quiz.why: set -u makes an unset variable an error, preventing empty expansions from silently changing a command.

options: It preserves each argument as a separate word
quiz.why: Quoted "$@" preserves word boundaries, which matters for arguments containing spaces or glob characters.

quiz.q: A script prints an error but exits 0. Why is that a problem?
options: Automation will treat the run as successful
quiz.why: Exit status is how callers detect failure. Printing an error without a non-zero exit hides the failure from automation.
